hhstaw-s995-f20-21.summary: Advice to keep the general command of the defence ("beim commendo maintenirt"); if age weighs, to withdraw as an "emeritus miles"; a plan for the command of the relief forces is "nicht practicabel vnd gantz immature".
hhstaw-s995-f20-21.en: [A] and I have read Your Dilection’s letter with care and attention and weighed it thoroughly, [to see] what we might best advise you in such weighty matters. We hold, first, that no one is fitter or more capable for this service than Your Dilection, since you understand the work of territorial defence (Landrettungswerk) thoroughly, have put it into practice for many years in a praiseworthy and most profitable way, and know better than anyone the state of the country and the temper of the whole levy (Auszug) and of the other levies, on which the preservation of the Lower [Q] will partly depend;

hhstaw-s995-f41.summary: Answer to Johann's defence plan for the Lower [Q]: militia plus a regular corps, muster by Circles, no invasion towards the Weser this year, provisions and artillery train.
hhstaw-s995-f41.en: [A] and I find the proposal that Your Dilection made to the [B] about preparing for war in the Lower [Q] weighty and well founded, and hold it a necessity to rely in part on the country militia (Landvolk), since good foreign troops are hard to get and such costs are more safely spent to the profit of the levy (Auszug). We think, however, that a good corps [M] would be most necessary in so extraordinary an expedition and against the multitude of different nations on the other side; this has been thought of […] from afar. It would also be desirable that, as soon as the enemy begins to assemble, all members of the Union should likewise bring their assistance together in one place;

hhstaw-s995-f44.summary: Hopes Johann will continue in his charge; dangerous to write such matters "ohne chifer"; [V] Portuguese coming into the [Q].
hhstaw-s995-f44.en: Now this has come to me almost against all expectation […], because in your last letter you made known quite a different opinion; and although, after [A] and I had read your letter and your reflections, one cannot blame you for seeking to free yourself from so doubtful an affair, yet since the common good, the [B] and your reputation are notably concerned, we should like satisfaction to be given you and you to continue in the charge entrusted to you, which we consider to be for the greatest service of the [B], and right too that they should meet you fairly in it and that you enjoy the fruits of the services faithfully rendered for [W] years now. We will nevertheless think further about the matter and send you our advice at the earliest. We find it very dangerous, however, to write such important and far-reaching matters over here without cipher (“ohne chifer”);

hhstaw-s995-f53.summary: Officers' yearly pay fixed by the late Elector; table money in actual service in the field, in the absence of the Margrave.
hhstaw-s995-f53.en: Your Dilection’s letter makes me doubt whether [the officers] have, besides the [∇] florins fixed by the late Elector as yearly pay, florins for allowance as well; in which case I hold that, if they were in actual service in the field, they should always be allowed enough to keep their table according to their quality and office, especially in the absence of the Lord Margrave, as is fitting […] (the line runs to the edge of the leaf).
